title: Edge Relay onboarding SLA and runbook for intermittent air-gapped/private VPC customers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and ship a customer-facing pattern (Edge Relay) and an associated onboarding SLA/runbook for customers with intermittent air-gapped or very constrained egress windows. The Edge Relay is an outbound-only lightweight connector that customers deploy in a DMZ or bastion subnet to allow scheduled upgrades, telemetry uploads, and certificate rotation without opening inbound ports. This ticket covers the product scope, acceptance criteria, high-level UX for Console, required security signoffs, and a lightweight engagement SLA for self-serve vs assisted onboarding.
acceptance_criteria: Spec document describing Edge Relay architecture, security model, and failure modes is approved by Security (confluence link in attachments)
Console UX: onboarding flow with three lanes (Self-serve: Fast Window, Scheduled Assisted, Concierge) implemented as mockups and signoff from Design
Runbook: step-by-step customer instructions for deploying Edge Relay (Docker/Helm/Windows service) and a verification checklist (connectivity probe, cert validation) published
SLA: documented response/triage times and handoffs for each lane (self-serve <48h, assisted <8h, concierge <2h during paid support window)
Compatibility matrix that lists supported OS/container runtimes, required outbound ports, TLS requirements, and expected egress bandwidth
Prototype repo with CI smoke tests and sample manifests available in GitHub (link in attachments)
Automation: ability for Console to register an Edge Relay agent ID via temporary token exchange (no inbound), and show agent health in Console dashboard
notes: Motivation: multiple enterprise customers requested a pattern that avoids inbound tunnels and meets strict egress-only networking policies. Existing bridge/proxy proposals rely on long-lived tunnels which violate some customer's policies.
Scope exclusions: this ticket does not include a fully-managed bastion host offering, nor does it include deep packet inspection or full mesh connectivity between customer sites.

Security posture: Edge Relay must support customer-provided TLS certs and integrate with KMS for key handling in private deployments. Audit logging must record manifest/apply events and upload artifacts to customer's S3 or local storage if requested.

Trade-offs considered: outbound-only reduces attack surface and legal complexity but limits live debugger access. To mitigate, we will implement rich offline telemetry bundles and a bi-directional short-lived command channel initiated from the customer to Redwood for on-demand troubleshooting (subject to approval).
